steps.title: Classify acuity and severity
steps.body: Chronic hyponatremia (>48 hours or unknown) carries ODS risk. Severe symptoms: seizures, coma, respiratory arrest.
steps.tip: Acute symptomatic hyponatremia can be corrected faster initially.

steps.title: Symptomatic severe — bolus
steps.body: Give 3% saline 100–150 mL over 10–20 minutes. Repeat up to twice if symptoms persist. Raise Na+ by ~2–4 mEq/L quickly.
steps.tip: Goal is symptom relief, not normalization.

steps.title: 24-hour correction limit
steps.body: In chronic hyponatremia, do not exceed 8–10 mEq/L rise in 24 hours (some guidelines use 8 mEq/L in high-risk patients).
steps.tip: ODS risk rises with faster correction — especially in alcoholism, malnutrition, hypokalemia.

steps.title: 48-hour limit
steps.body: Total correction should not exceed 18 mEq/L in 48 hours. Recheck sodium every 2–4 hours during active correction.

steps.title: Definitive management
steps.body: Fluid restriction for SIADH, treat hypovolemia with saline, stop offending drugs, and address adrenal/thyroid disease.
steps.tip: Uric acid low and urine osm >100 support SIADH.
